audit.summary: The class-gradient formula omits the severity-squared factor from the normalization denominator. An exact finite-support population satisfies both printed covariance conditions but reverses the promised derivative sign; the automatically differentiated implementation and reported accuracy are not thereby refuted.

proposition.claim: The theorem gives nonnegative class-weight gradient when \(\sigma^2\ge\|b\|^2/(4d_{\rm irr})\) and \(\sigma^2\ge\|c\|^2/(4d_{\rm noise})\), where \(c=\operatorname{Cov}(v^{\rm noise},\hat y)\) already includes noise severity.

repair.content: The noise bracket must be \(4\sigma^2s^2d_{\rm noise}-\|c\|^2\), giving sufficient condition \(\sigma^2\ge\|c\|^2/(4s^2d_{\rm noise})\) for positive severity/dimension. Quotient differentiation also gives shift derivative \(-2V(\mathbf1)s^2\delta^2/D_0\); its nonpositive sign survives the coefficient correction. Zero severity or absent components need separate omission rather than division by zero.
